{{Top}}
[[File:AnakinSkywalker-SWBC52cvr.png|thumb|250px|[[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], nicknamed the '''Hero With No Fear'''.]]
{{Quote|Somebody's got to be the poster boy.|[[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] to Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (novelization)">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref>}}
The title '''"Hero With No Fear"''' was one of many monikers given to [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (novelization)" /> Following his exploits during the Battles of [[Battle of Jabiim|Jabiim]] and [[Battle of Aargonar (Clone Wars)|Aargonar]],<ref name="TNEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]] features commonly referred to Skywalker using this nickname, turning him into a poster boy for the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] war effort.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (novelization)" />

Despite this nickname, Skywalker himself was plagued by the fear of failure, pain and loss, and delved into the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]] in an attempt to attain further power and quash his fear. As [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader, he initially considered himself to truly be the Hero With No Fear, but after realizing the cost of his newfound power&mdash;the [[Death/Legends|death]] of [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] and his injuries [[Duel on Mustafar/Legends|suffered]] on [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]]&mdash;he came to understand he would always carry fear with him.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (novelization)" />

==Behind the scenes==
The 20th anniversary deluxe edition of [[Matthew Stover]]'s [[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]] features an addendum titled The Sun-Dragon Crisis in which he explains that the [[Sun-dragon/Legends|sun-dragon]] motif used throughout the novel to represent Anakin's fear is not that which appeared in his original manuscript, but a revision which came about only after he truly understood why the script of the film had tagged him as the "Hero with No Fear," that it was dramatic irony. In a footnote elsewhere in the novel, he explains that he had originally believed Anakin's main struggle to be with his anger, that he naturally assumed that rage was most of what drove him. Upon waking in [[Darth Vader's armor/Legends|his armor]], Vader himself has the revelation that the "dragon" never existed, that it was himself all along.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (novelization)" />
